Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept. Create ONE landscape 16:10 game screenshot concept for a modest, achievable Three.js browser arena shooter. This will appear on the LEFT of a Chinese PDF describing a first-time player's journey. It is a proposed game screen, not a cinematic illustration.
SCENE: a compact outdoor practice corner of a small mint-green playground arena, viewed from a fixed elevated three-quarter / top-down camera, 50 degrees downward. Orthographic-like perspective, ground fills the image. Short cream rectangular walls, two wood crates, one red/white circular target on a simple stand, a few low polygon round bushes at the edge. Clear walking space and visible paths. No buildings or complex architecture.
PLAYER: a cute Nailong-inspired chubby bright yellow baby dinosaur, big oval belly, short tiny arms, short legs, tiny tail, rounded head, large simple black eyes, open cheerful mouth, small pale belly patch. Simple low-poly rounded mesh, no fur, no clothing except a BLUE neckerchief identifying the player. Character height about 7 percent of screenshot. It holds a small toy bubble blaster. One visible round cyan projectile travels toward the target. A green flat circular player marker under the character.
STYLE: plausible indie student-project real-time 3D screenshot. Low-poly meshes, flat pastel materials, one directional daylight, simple contact/blob shadows. Crisp geometry. No ray tracing, no photorealism, no cinematic depth of field, no volumetric fog, no huge particle effects, no fancy water, no detailed vegetation. Cheerful but restrained, very readable gameplay.
UI: minimal clean actual game HUD. Top left a small rounded dark teal badge with exactly “练习场”. Bottom left a simple health bar and “100”. Bottom center a compact key hint with exactly “W A S D” and “移动”, then a mouse icon and “射击”, then “SPACE” and “冲刺”. Top right a small gear icon. No browser chrome, no extra text, no paragraph, no large title, no watermark. All text sharp and legible.
Keep the entire screen in a usable screenshot composition, no poster framing.
